lean.fidelity_note:
Let $J$ be an interval on which relative time derivatives are unique. The formal statement assumes a differentiable spatial linear map $D(t)$ with $\operatorname{tr}D=0$ and symmetric $D'+D^2$, together with $k'=-D^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any primitive $P'=F$, it proves that $u(t,x)=D(t)x+\mathbf a(t)F(k(t)\cdot x)$ is divergence free and satisfies the Euler momentum equation on $\mathbb R^3$ whenever $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$ throughout $J$. The pressure is exactly $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$. The needed time and spatial differentiability of the velocity and spatial differentiability of the pressure are included. If $k,\mathbf a$ are nonzero and perpendicular at one $t_0\in J$, these properties persist at every $t\in J$, including times before $t_0$.

The paper assumes smooth $D$, a smooth odd one-periodic profile with $F'(0)=1$, and a primitive of zero phase average. The formal statement does not require those additional profile properties or the higher regularity of $D$. It also extends the Euler-identity part to $k=0$, where the coefficient is assigned zero by the convention that division by zero is zero. The persistence part still explicitly requires nonzero initial data. These are precise extensions of the quoted lemma, not a change from periodic Euler dynamics to an affine torus flow: this lemma concerns the local affine model on $\mathbb R^3$.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1

statements.markdown: Let $D(t)$ be smooth and trace free, with $D'+D^2$ symmetric. Then $Dx$ solves the Euler equations with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2$. Choose a smooth odd $1$-periodic profile $F$ with $F'(0)=1$, and let $P'=F$, $\langle P\rangle_s=0$. Here $\langle H\rangle_s=\int_0^1H(s)\,\mathrm ds$ is the phase average.
statements.section: 2.1 Exact waves over a linear background
